As at November 2026, Smartraveller's 'Getting married overseas' page (last updated 18/08/2026, read live 11 November 2026, unchanged from paros-wedding-venues fact_302) says some countries ask you to prove you are free to marry, most commonly with a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and certificates from a registry of births, deaths and marriages (a statement of no record of a previous marriage, a Single Status certificate or a No Record Result certificate); local authorities may also ask for divorce papers, a deceased spouse's death certificate, and your original birth certificate and passport. DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their country, so ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether you need a CNI, whether you can get it in Australia, and whether it also needs an authentication or apostille. It says each country decides what proof it accepts and there may be different regional and national laws. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller (read live 11 November 2026, unchanged from paros-wedding-venues fact_303) says you cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if, when it took place, it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law had it occurred in Australia. A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage but may not work as proof of a name change (check with your local registry of births, deaths and marriages), and Smartraveller suggests talking to a lawyer to confirm the certificate is valid in Australia. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller (read live 11 November 2026) says Australia does not recognise overseas marriages where one or both people are already married to someone else, not old enough to marry, too closely related, or forced to marry.

An appointment is needed for all notarial services (Monday to Friday, 9:00am to 12:30pm), though apostille and CNI documents can be submitted by post; apostilled documents and CNIs are available for collection within two working days unless same-day collection is arranged in advance, or can be returned by mail. Kapari Natural Resort's Weddings & Ceremonies page says it helps couples plan and hold their wedding ceremony and reception, provides a dedicated wedding planner, and accepts events 'for up to approx. 30 people'.

Ambassador Aegean Luxury Hotel & Suites (Akrotiri; not Grand Ambassador) home page: 'Perched on the edge of the cliff, overlooking the imposing caldera and the emblematic volcano of Santorini, Ambassador Aegean Luxury Hotel & Suites welcomes you to Akrotiri.'

Ambassador Aegean home page has a 'WEDDING & HONEYMOON' section reading 'Organize a Fairytale Wedding & Magical Honeymoon', and its footer menu lists 'WEDDINGS & HONEYMOONS'. The linked wedding page (/wedding-honeymoons-santorini-hotel/) returned a 404 on 2026-11-12, so no ceremony options, capacity or wedding services are published in a readable page.

Ambassador Aegean home page: 'Our luxury hotel in Santorini offers 40 suites, villas & rooms with private pools' (meta description; body: '40 private pools, one waiting for you'). Signature details named: a private helipad and golf cars for moving around the property. It describes Akrotiri as 'one of Santorini's least exploited areas', a few minutes from the ancient settlement.

Vedema, a Luxury Collection Resort (Megalochori) weddings page: 'Host your wedding in one of our spectacular venues and exchange your vows within a scenery of a traditional Cycladic village.' Ceremonies 'at the resort, on the beach, or elsewhere'; receptions at the Pool Restaurant or, for more privacy, the Canava Wine Bar; a private beach bonfire and barbecue are options.

Vedema home page describes a 400-year-old winery turned Cycladic village retreat in medieval Megalochori, 'surrounded by emerald vineyards'. The only caldera wording is for one villa: 'Hidden away in the Megalochori Caldera, Nafsika Estate combines absolute privacy, spectacular views...' (350 sq.m., private helipad). No caldera VIEW is stated in words for the resort or its wedding spaces, so Vedema does not meet part 2 of the inclusion rule.

Vedema's official Marriott events page says the 400-year-old Wine Cellar can hold up to 120 guests for a banquet and 150 for a reception, and that Vedema provides wedding services (Celebration Consultant). Used only as context; Vedema is not qualified (no caldera view wording).

Katikies Garden (Fira) home page: a five-star hotel with 40 suites in a converted monastery in the heart of Fira. Its caldera wording is about the town, not the hotel: 'Fira is situated on the island's famed Caldera... it promises stunning views and splendid sunsets.' Its FAQ says 'Some of our suites offer sea views, whereas 180° views are offered from the infinity pool'. No caldera view is stated for the property in words, so it does not meet part 2 of the inclusion rule on this read.

Aria Suites (Fira): its home page meta description says 'Explore luxurious suites and villas, spectacular caldera views, private jacuzzis'; its schema says 'an elite boutique hotel in Fira with a view of the volcano and the historic Acrotiri' and gives a 4-star rating. Its Facilities & Services page lists 'Wedding planning' among services. No wedding spaces, ceremony options or capacity are published.

Gavalas Winery (Megalochori) home page: family boutique winery, one of the oldest on Santorini, five generations. The home page mentions neither weddings nor a caldera view, so it does not meet the inclusion rule on this read.

Santorini Gem's home page is headed 'Your Wedding in Santorini Gem' and says 'The majestic caldera views will make a perfect backdrop to your very special moment, while Santorini Gem Wedding Venue and Villa will enchant your guests.' It describes a private estate 'with the flawless views and the wonderful green spaces for the celebration of your marriage'.

Santorini Gem's home page says the venue 'is able to host large or smaller-scale events, with outdoor and indoor spaces, selected services and a variety of menus', offers wedding planning services, and frames 'an emotional ceremony to unfold at sunset'. Its ceremony and reception teaser reads 'Exchange vows in the Caldera among friends and family. Celebrate your special day with a dinner party!'

Santorini Gem's venue page lists 'An incredible ceremony venue facing the volcanos, a dining area and a cosy bar, a large pool overlooking the famous Caldera with wonderful poolside areas and an imposing luxury wedding villa', and refers to 'the imposing caldera views'. No guest capacity figure appears on the pages read (a venue policy PDF and rental brochure are linked but were not read).

Santorini Gem's villa page says 'Perched on the legendary caldera cliffs of Santorini, Gem Villa is a private sanctuary', with 'five elegant bedrooms accommodating up to eight guests', four bathrooms, two living rooms, a private pool facing the horizon and gardens.
Santorini Gem's contact block gives the address only as 'GEM, Santorini, Cyclades, Greece'; the pages read do not name the village or area.

Erosantorini's estate page describes an 'exclusive-use estate' with 'panoramic views of Santorini's iconic villages, dazzling sunsets, and the legendary caldera', five suites for up to ten guests on two acres, located 'on the edge of the caldera in the Messaria area, just 2 kilometers south of Santorini's bustling capital, Fira'. The home page lists a private chapel and an 'Events' heading but no wedding wording on the pages read, so it does not yet meet the inclusion rule.

Kivotos Santorini's home page says it is 'Built high atop the cliffside in Imerovigli, the most exclusive spot on the caldera' and the Signature Suite offers 'panoramic views of the island's breathtaking caldera'. No wedding wording appears on the home page, so it does not meet the inclusion rule on this read.

Cavo Tagoo Santorini's home page says it is 'Set between breathtaking Caldera views and an iconic infinity pool' and its concierge list includes 'SPECIAL OCCASION PLANNING'; the word wedding does not appear on the page read, so it does not meet the inclusion rule.

Perivolas (Oia) says it 'boasts a prime cliffside location overlooking the Caldera' (home) and 'with its stunning Caldera views' (contact page); neither page mentions weddings, so it does not meet the inclusion rule on this read.
Esperas (Oia) describes its Ombra Restaurant with 'spectacular views of the Caldera'; the home and hotel pages read do not mention weddings, so it does not meet the inclusion rule on this read.

Celestia Grand's home page says 'Gaze beyond the horizon, where the caldera's majesty meets refined elegance' and calls itself the 'Most easily accessible caldera hotel'; no wedding wording appears on the home page, so it does not meet the inclusion rule on this read.

insider_details.detail: Oia's caldera-edge ceremony spaces are intimate (Canaves Panorama Balcony 30, Veranda 40, Sunset Terrace 25 as wedding spaces; Katikies Botrini's 60 seated), so a guest list beyond about 60 points to a buyout of a larger property such as Canaves Epitome (max 170 guests) or a split between ceremony and reception spaces.
Canaves Sunset Terrace is listed for 25 guests as a wedding space but 100 reception in the buyout table: confirm which figure applies to your package before you cap the guest list.
Katikies Santorini only accepts children over 13, so families with young children need Katikies Garden in Fira or another hotel for those guests.
Use separate spaces for each event: Canaves Epitome names a Sunset Terrace for the ceremony and the Sunset Pool Lounge for cocktails and dinner, which keeps the evening moving without a venue change.

Imerovigli's cliff-top wedding spaces are small: Grace's two spaces seat 40 and 15, so a seated dinner above about 40 needs a second venue or a larger property; plan guest numbers before shortlisting.
Grace requires an independent wedding planner engaged at least 3 months out, so budget planner time from the booking date, not just the wedding week.
For guests with limited mobility, ask each cliffside venue about steps; Le Ciel is the only venue in this batch that states road access, very few steps and wheelchair ramps.
Astra Suites publishes no wedding capacity or ceremony terms online, so treat it as an intimate or elopement option and confirm numbers with the hotel before promising guests rooms.

Santo Wines and Venetsanos Winery are both wineries with caldera-facing terraces, so a sunset ceremony and a wine-led reception can sit in one place; Venetsanos publishes terrace capacity (about 100 seated), Santo Wines does not, so ask its Event Manager early.
Aroma Suites suits elopements and micro weddings only: its rooftop ceremony space takes up to 15-20 guests, and a larger group means a hotel buyout plus rooms at a nearby property.
Katikies Garden's entrance is reachable only on foot, so plan luggage and guest access in Fira if it is used as a guest base.

Tholos Resort sits on the Imerovigli cliff and frames its weddings around the volcano and the white villages along the caldera rim, with sunset as the backdrop, so build the ceremony time around sunset and confirm the exact terrace in the Wedding Packages PDF.

Tholos says it can plan a chapel ceremony facing the volcano, a beach wedding or one on its own premises, so couples can split the ceremony off-site and keep the reception at the hotel; transfers between chapel and hotel are a planning item for the Wedded Advisor.

Kapari has 17 rooms and suites and an in-house event planning team, so a small wedding party can stay, marry and dine in one place in Imerovigli; confirm guest numbers and the ceremony terrace with the venue, as capacity is not published.

Katikies Chromata sits on the highest point of Imerovigli with 180-degree, direct sunset views and a top-level Aperitivo Bar, and welcomes children over 13 only, which matters for families bringing younger guests.
Ambassador Aegean sits on the Akrotiri cliffs in the quieter south-west of the island, so guests who want Fira or Oia evenings will need to plan the drive.
Santorini Gem pairs the event spaces with a five-bedroom villa for up to eight, so the couple and closest family can stay where the wedding happens; everyone else needs rooms elsewhere.
Santorini Gem frames the ceremony at sunset facing the volcano; a sunset ceremony means the reception runs after dark, so lighting and guest travel back to hotels need planning.
